our_argument_summary: The dome cites the 2009 July 22 East Asian eclipse Chinese gravimeter-network null ('Sun 2010'; closest verified record Wen, Tang, Wang, Gao & Hua 2013, CJG 56(3):770-782, doi:10.6038/cjg20130306) as confirming the model. But the dome's own published coupling kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal (WIN-012, monitor.py Domain #7) converts the documented totality magnetic perturbation (5-15 nT, Kim & Chang 2018 ensemble) into a predicted 3-9 uGal contact-phase gravity pulse at the network. The network recorded no such signal. The dome's own published mechanism failed its own cited data: Refuted by Data. Coverage-scaling defender pivots are foreclosed by (a) kappa's published status as an unconditioned constant and (b) arithmetic survival of linear/quadratic scaling at the off-totality sites.

holes_found.description: The instrument-composition hedge is now obsolete and factually wrong in its disclaimer. Our prose says the campaign was 'approximately eight superconducting/spring gravimeters across roughly six Chinese sites' and explicitly states 'we have not located an independent English-language verification of the precise instrument or site totals.' The cited record's own English abstract (read this cycle at the doi.org-resolved geophy.cn page) states the exact composition: 'seven LaCoste-Romberg gravimeters and one SG-053 superconducting gravimeter.' The verification we claim not to have located is in the very source we cite. A defender who clicks our own DOI finds us hedging about a fact printed in the abstract - sloppiness that taxes credibility on an otherwise-strong WIN.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the hedge with the exact composition: 'seven LaCoste-Romberg spring gravimeters and one SG-053 superconducting gravimeter (per the record's English abstract)'. Drop the 'we have not located an independent English-language verification' parenthetical entirely. Mirror the fix in tldr_evidence ('approximately eight superconducting/spring gravimeters across roughly six sites' -> 'seven spring gravimeters and one superconducting gravimeter'). Site count: the abstract does not give a site total; keep 'roughly six sites' hedged or drop it.

holes_found.description: Instrument-precision smear: the prose attributes '0.1-1 uGal post-reduction precision (Crossley, Hinderer & Riccardi 2013)' to 'The Chinese SG network' as a whole, but Crossley et al. is a superconducting-gravimeter precision reference and only ONE of the eight instruments (SG-053) was superconducting; seven were LaCoste-Romberg springs. Worse, our own WIN-011/WIN-012 prose argues the Mohe 6.5-uGal anomaly is plausibly a thermal-tilt artifact of exactly this spring-instrument class. A defender can compile the two statements: 'Your review says LCR springs are thermally unreliable when attacking kappa's denominator, then quietly assigns them SG-class 0.1-1 uGal precision when using the 2009 null.' The cross-WIN tension is real even though the refutation survives it (the on-path 3-9 uGal prediction exceeds even LCR post-fit floors of ~1-2 uGal).
holes_found.recommendation: Scope the precision claim: '...the single SG-053 superconducting gravimeter sampling at 0.1-1 uGal post-reduction precision (Crossley, Hinderer & Riccardi 2013), flanked by seven LaCoste-Romberg springs whose post-fit residual floors (~1-2 uGal) still sit well below the 3-9 uGal on-path prediction.' Optionally add: the precision asymmetry cuts against the dome - if the springs are too noisy to trust, the dome's Mohe denominator (same instrument class) falls with them. Verification follow-up for analyst: pull the CJG full text's station table to determine which site hosted SG-053; if it sat on or near the totality corridor, say so - it makes the campaign's best instrument the on-path one and closes the 'maybe the SG was off-path' escape.

holes_found.description: Quote-minable sensitivity language unaddressed: our prose says the network 'recorded zero across all sites' and 'measured zero', adopting the dome's '0.0 uGal' characterization. The verified record's abstract actually concludes 'the supposed gravity anomaly during the total solar eclipse cannot be detected at present with actual observation conditions and instrument performance' - phrasing a defender will quote as a SENSITIVITY statement ('the instruments couldn't have seen it') rather than a clean null. We should preempt with the dilemma, which is fatal either way: (a) if the result is a clean zero (the dome's own 'CONFIRMED 0.0 uGal across network' framing), kappa's 3-9 uGal prediction is refuted - our current argument; (b) if the result is 'insufficient sensitivity', then the dome's WIN-014 evaporates on the dome's own terms - a non-detection at insufficient sensitivity cannot 'confirm electromagnetic not gravitational' and cannot 'replicate WIN-013'. And reading (b) is not actually available for the on-path stations anyway, since 3-9 uGal exceeds even the spring-instrument post-fit floor.
holes_found.recommendation: Add two sentences after the 'recorded zero' sentence: quote the abstract's conclusion verbatim, then state the dilemma - either the dome's own 0.0-uGal framing stands and kappa is refuted by it, or the campaign lacked sensitivity and WIN-014 confirms nothing; the dome cannot keep the WIN under either reading. This converts the strongest remaining defender quote-mine into a second vise.

holes_found.description: The '~30% floor threshold' claim is conservative in our favor but imprecise as stated: 'only sites at coverages below ~30% would fall to the floor.' At 30% linear scaling the predicted range is 0.89-2.68 uGal - only the bottom edge enters the 0.1-1 uGal floor band; the upper edge stays above the floor down to ~11% coverage (1.677/15 = 0.112). The sentence understates our case and a pedantic critic could call the 30% figure unmotivated in either direction.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional tightening: 'only sites below roughly 30% coverage even begin to graze the floor at the low-dB end, and the full predicted range stays above the floor down to about 11% coverage.' Low priority; the current phrasing harms nothing.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's own WIN-014 source disavows kappa's denominator: the 2013 CJG paper's English abstract concludes that 'the previous anomaly was very likely created by the drastic changes in the weather.' The 'previous anomaly' is the Mohe-class eclipse gravity signal - and Mohe 1997's 6.5 uGal IS the denominator of kappa = 10.9/6.5 (WIN-012, monitor.py Domain #7). So the very paper the dome cites as confirming WIN-014 attributes the empirical basis of the dome's coupling constant to weather artifacts. This is independent, dome-cited-source corroboration of our existing WIN-011/012 thermal-tilt argument, and it is currently nowhere on our site (grep of wins.json and sections.json for the weather attribution: absent). It belongs in the kappa-cluster vise and as a sentence in WIN-014.

Authorship continuity: Wang Qian-Shen, lead claimant of the 1997 Mohe eclipse gravity anomaly (Wang, Yang & Tang 2001, Chinese Science Bulletin 46(12) - already in the CJG paper's own reference list), is a co-author of the 2013 null paper. The original anomaly's own research group ran the better 2009 campaign, found nothing, and attributed the earlier signal to weather. 'The people who found the Mohe anomaly retracted it themselves' is rhetorically far stronger than 'a later paper found a null.'

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly reports a genuine, high-quality null: the 2009 campaign (doi:10.6038/cjg20130306) - 'seven LaCoste-Romberg gravimeters and one SG-053 superconducting gravimeter', described by its own abstract as possibly 'the best research activity both in the experiment scale and in the observation quality in the past century' - found no eclipse gravity anomaly. That null is real science and genuinely refutes Majorana-style gravitational-shielding claims at the uGal scale (cjg20130306 abstract; data/wins.json:WIN-014 detail_evidence).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A null only confirms a model that predicted a null. The dome simultaneously publishes kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal as a locked constant (live monitor.py Domain #7, lines 477-489; 08-live-power.txt:160 'Constants Locked') which converts its own cited eclipse magnetic perturbations (5-15 nT; doi:10.1016/j.asr.2018.01.022) into a 3-9 uGal pulse the 2009 network should have seen. The same null the dome claims as confirmation is a refutation of the dome's own published coupling - and the paper's weather attribution simultaneously dissolves kappa's Mohe denominator (cjg20130306 abstract conclusion).

advocate_mode.best_defense: As a dome defender accepting your review's own principles: (1) Your noise-floor citation (Crossley 2013) covers superconducting gravimeters, but the record you yourselves verified says seven of the eight instruments were LaCoste-Romberg springs - the exact instrument class YOUR review calls thermally unreliable in WIN-011/012. (2) The paper's own conclusion is that the anomaly 'cannot be detected at present with actual observation conditions and instrument performance' - the campaign authors themselves frame this as an instrument-sensitivity limit, not a measured zero. (3) You have not shown where the single high-precision SG-053 actually sat; if it was off the totality corridor, the only instrument with a sub-uGal floor never saw totality, and the on-path 'zero' rests on springs whose thermal response during eclipse contacts your own review elsewhere treats as artifact-generating. So the network null is an absence of evidence at uncertain sensitivity, not evidence of absence at 0.1 uGal.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Patch holes 2 and 3 together: scope the Crossley precision claim to SG-053, state the LCR post-fit floor (~1-2 uGal) explicitly and note 3-9 uGal clears it, quote the abstract's 'cannot be detected' conclusion and run the either-way dilemma (clean zero -> kappa refuted; insufficient sensitivity -> WIN-014 confirms nothing and the dome's '0.0 uGal CONFIRMED' framing collapses). Ask analyst to extract the CJG full-text station table to pin SG-053's location. The defense never threatens the verdict - under its strongest form WIN-014 still cannot be a dome confirmation - but it can score rhetorical points against our current wording.

deeper_analysis: This cycle's drift was the decider's clean integration of all five c11 recommendations - every one verified present in the current prose (Wuhan in-corridor naming; 50%/~30% low-coverage bracketing; quadratic parenthetical; hedged vise; tiered city list) and every number in the new text reproduces arithmetically. The patch closed c11's holes without introducing errors; c11's H1-H5 are all resolved, so unresolved_prior_cycle is empty. The fresh findings come from going one source-layer deeper than any prior cycle: resolving the CJG DOI and reading the English abstract directly. That single fetch yields (a) the exact instrument composition (7 LCR + 1 SG-053), which obsoletes our 'no English-language verification located' hedge and exposes the SG-class-precision smear; (b) the 'cannot be detected at present' conclusion language, which is the strongest remaining defender quote-mine and converts cleanly into a second vise; and (c) the weather attribution of the 'previous anomaly', which is the dome's own cited source disavowing kappa's Mohe denominator - the single best new argument available to the kappa cluster, currently absent from the site. Also strengthened this cycle: monitoring tag validated against the dome's LIVE monitor.py (fetched from john09289/predictions) rather than our raw-text snapshot - no WIN-014 domain exists in current code, and Domain #7's kappa check is hardcoded arithmetic on two baked-in historical values (10.9, 6.5). The verdict is robust: under every defender reading examined (coverage scaling linear/quadratic, instrument-sensitivity retreat, off-path SG), WIN-014 either refutes kappa or stops being evidence for the dome. Recommended action is minor_edit (holes 1-3 are wording-level patches, no structural rework); suggest the decider route the station-table extraction (SG-053 location) to the analyst as a small verification EXP since it requires the Chinese full text.
